question: For Nintendo's first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027 (April 1 - June 30, 2026), what were net sales and operating profit in yen, how much did Nintendo say it recorded as a reduction of cost of sales from refunds of U.S. IEEPA tariffs, and - converting that refund at the quarter's average rate of JPY 159.38 per US dollar - what was operating profit excluding the refund and how did it compare with the prior-year quarter's JPY 56.9 billion?
grading: Key points (all required): (1) net sales JPY 517.8 billion (-9.5% y/y); (2) operating profit JPY 142.5 billion (+150.5%; prior-year JPY 56.9 billion); (3) tariff refund approximately US$300 million recorded as a reduction of cost of sales; (4) at JPY 159.38/USD the refund is about JPY 47.8 billion, so operating profit excluding it is about JPY 94.7 billion (accept JPY 92-97 billion), roughly +66% versus JPY 56.9 billion (accept +62% to +70%). The answer must flag the conversion as an approximation. Fail if the quarter is mislabelled (e.g., Jan-Mar 2027), if the refund is treated as a yen figure disclosed by Nintendo, or if operating profit ex-refund is not computed.
answer: Q1 FY3/2027 (April 1-June 30, 2026): net sales JPY 517.8 billion (-9.5%) and operating profit JPY 142.5 billion (+150.5% from JPY 56.9 billion). Nintendo said it recorded approximately US$300 million as a reduction of cost of sales for refunds of IEEPA tariffs [W11-E1]. At the average rate of JPY 159.38/USD that is about JPY 47.8 billion, so operating profit excluding the refund is about JPY 94.7 billion, still about +66% y/y. The full-year forecast (operating profit JPY 370.0 billion) was unchanged from May [W11-E1]. Switch 2 hardware sold 3.82 million units in the quarter [W11-E1].

output.answer:
**Nintendo FY27/Q1 (April 1 – June 30, 2026) — reported August 6, 2026**

| Metric | FY27/Q1 | FY26/Q1 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | ¥517.8 bn | ¥572.3 bn | −9.5% |
| Operating profit | ¥142.5 bn | ¥56.9 bn | +150.5% |
| Ordinary profit | ¥206.1 bn | ¥95.8 bn | +115.1% |
| Profit attributable to owners of parent | ¥147.4 bn | ¥96.0 bn | +53.5% |

**IEEPA tariff refund:** Nintendo recorded "approximately 300 million U.S. dollars as a reduction of cost of sales in connection with refunds of IEEPA tariffs," noting the tariffs involved "were primarily borne by the company rather than passed on to consumers through product prices." (It was the U.S. Supreme Court striking down the IEEPA duties that triggered the refunds.)

**Converting at the quarter's average rate of ¥159.38/USD:**
- $300M × ¥159.38 = **≈ ¥47.8 billion** (¥47.814 bn)

**Operating profit excluding the refund:**
- ¥142.5 bn − ¥47.8 bn = **≈ ¥94.7 billion** (¥94.69 bn)

**Versus prior-year quarter (¥56.9 bn):**
- 94.69 / 56.9 = 1.664 → **up ~66.4% year over year**, an increase of roughly **¥37.8 billion**
- So even stripped of the one-time tariff windfall, operating profit still grew by about two-thirds, driven by a richer software mix (digital sales +90% to ¥132.7 bn) and IP-related income (+107.4% to ¥34.8 bn) — as opposed to the reported +150.5%.

Sources:
- Nintendo, "Financial Results Explanatory Material, 1st Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 2027" (Aug 6, 2026): https://www.nintendo.co.jp/ir/pdf/2026/260806_2e.pdf
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nintendo-q1-operating-profit-jumps-151-beating-analyst-estimates-2026-08-06
- GamesIndustry.biz: https://www.gamesindustry.biz/nintendo-q1-sales-drop-95-operating-profit-soars-following-higher-software-sales-and-300m-in-us-tariff-refunds

*Note: figures are approximate since Nintendo disclosed the refund as "approximately $300 million," and sources round operating profit to either ¥142.5 bn or ¥142.6 bn.*
